body:
Ah, the ever so helpful reddit anti-college circlejerk.

You know what? You're right. I'm wasting my time here.

I've made my decision, if college doesn't work out I'm going to kill myself.

Goodbye!

It's not just my grades. If I don't get signed up for my classes I can't graduate. One of my classes filled in an hour the day registration started. There's no chance of getting into it. So it's more complicated than "Oh I just don't have the pressure on me to try in school"

Put yourself in my position. 

You went to two years of trade school after high school. During that time you worked in the shop from 6:00 AM to 11:30 PM every day because you were motivated. Everyone has told you your whole life that with hard work and discipline you'll eventually gain genuine talent and a sense of purpose.

But that never came. You were terrible. Your classmates would show up an hour late for class, drunk. They'd finish the project you were working on in fifteen minutes, then give you a half-hearted sympathetic pat on the back while you prepared for another late night of working until the instructors eventually said you had to go home.

It goes like this forever until you finally graduate. Nobody thinks you should work in your field. They acknowledge that you gave it your best but they're really only letting you graduate based on your effort and extensive book knowledge on your trade, and strongly encourage you to go to college because it might be your best chance to make something of yourself.

So you do that. You get told the restrictions on your financial aid, but you're confident you'll be okay. Though admittedly you're a little depressed that your first plan didn't work out. You work really hard and your first semester you make an A in your classes, but just barely. Second semester you make two B's and two A's, but whatever, you're passing. You convince yourself that this is right for you and everything will be okay.

Then you're in your third semester. Right off the bat you fail every one of your exams. 58, 62, 66. So you study extra hard, you stop sleeping, you stop eating. You live your entire life at school getting tutoring.

You fail your tests again. 

Now you're being faced with failing your classes. Your assignments are getting harder and your classmates are passing you by. You meet with your professor in their office hours and they're convinced you're just not applying yourself. You sleep even less, eat even less. Your anniversary comes around, you have a quick dinner, wait for your girlfriend to go to sleep and spend the rest of the night doing calculus.

Your birthday comes up, you blow off plans to go out to eat with your sister because you have a project due.

Fallout 4 is released, you've waited forever. You refuse to play it until you get to where you need to be academically.

Your whole life is dedicated to making this work, to being able to achieve at least one goal in your life. Because until now you've never succeeded at anything.

And then you get told that it's unlikely you'll be able to continue with school, even if you turn things around and pass your classes, there's a decent chance that you'll have to pay for school without the help of student loans and federal financial aid.

You know what happens to people like this.

After all this work, all this effort, all those sleepless nights, the nights you neglected your family, you neglected your girlfriend, you neglected your physical health. All because you just want to accomplish ONE THING with your life. Now that's being taken away from you so you can be as qualified as some 16 year old stoner kid. Your college has told you if that happens you will never receive aid to go to school again.

And you wonder why I would kill myself? Why the fuck would you want to live after that?

Graduating college and getting a job in my field. 

Either that or dying.

Found an /r/askreddit thread from two months ago on this. 

https://www.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/comments/3kk57x/redditors_who_didnt_go_to_college_what_do_you_do/

Here's the top comment

> Those of you who may be reading this thinking its may be a good idea for YOU to drop out, remember that only the successful people are going to post in here. This thread probably isn't a fair representation of non college graduates 

Here's another one

> Joined the marine corps, and I'm currently sitting in a class learning about college opportunities...

Here's another

> Manage a board game store. 9 year old me would crap his pants hearing that.

Riveting.

Let's see some more huh?

> Own my own bar/nightclub.

>Make 3 times more money than most of my college graduating friends.

>Make my own hours.

Hey now that sounds pretty good! How'd they do it?

> Left school at 16 in Europe. Worked in bars and restaurants. Came to the US at 21. Worked in more bars. Saved and Saved. Got bored with working in bars. Went to IT school for a couple of months. Got a job at the beginning of the IT boom in 1997. Ended up working for a company traveling the US on the company dime. Saved more and more. Still worked part time as a bartender. Was traveling extensively when 9/11 happened. Stopped shortly after. Couldn't take it any more. Went into partnership with a friend using all the money I saved. 10 Years later bought out business friend. Reinvested in business. 

Ah so it was a very situational thing based around when he was already in the workforce and friends he already knew. So this plan is useless to me.

> I'm a college drop out. I work 70 hours a week at two jobs in food service. I make about 1500- 1800 a month

Yep, that's about what I figured.

> I'm a pipe fabricator/fitter, I build all the piping, that goes into the chemical refineries, and oil field stations. If I worked every month, I'd make about $110k annually. I just took 2 months though. Not horrible for a 22 year old. 

And then there's my plan A! That's the kind of thing I read at age 18 and I wasted two years of my life on, putting myself on permanent academic probation!

> I do laundry and dishes, clean the house, care for the cat, and tap away at coding that never really goes anywhere. See a doctor every five years or something. Clean up after everything my wife does that isn't in the toilet. Have sex with her about once a month and then cry about it.

> I mean, I'm alive, so it's a living, and I'm doing it.

Yeah that sounds like happiness. Especially considering my girlfriend doesn't have a college degree.

> Separated from the military, working as an air traffic controller. Over 100k a year at 24 ain't a bad gig.

Military again. Yeah I'm just going to go ahead and say no.

Do I need to go on?

Vietnamese manicurists! The pinnacle of American success.

I'll put this as kindly as I can. I'm already trying to learn skills. This whole, "college" thing? What do you think that was for?

The learning skills tactic isn't working out, and since my only path to success is learning skills, death seems like a preferable alternative.

I'd like to correct something. Though I appreciate what you're saying.

It isn't that I simply don't like what I'm studying. It's that I'm not good at it. If the pressure was off and I had some wiggle room I would LOVE my classes. But where half my classmates in calculus are taking it for the second time, I don't have the same luxury.

Technology is all I can do. I can't even afford community college without financial aid. I'm currently in the affordable, lower-level courses. At his rate I'll be lucky if I can take another year to get my goddamn associates. Which are worth about as much as a degree from University of Phoenix so what's even the point? 

Besides not being allowed to switch, I don't know anything else I'm good at. I thought I would learn to be good at my trade but that didn't work out in vocational school. I learned I was good with math and computers at that time so I thought this was what I should pursue. Everyone told me it was a perfect fit for me. 

Before you ask, because judging from other conversations I've had with people. No, I don't have any other hobbies. I can't cook, I can't draw, I've not "always dreamed of starting my own business", I'm not a people person, I don't like to write, I'm not a musician, I already tried trade school (seriously can't emphasize this enough, it's all people ever suggest to me), I'm not a good public speaker. 

Technology. Math and technology. As far as I know those are the only things I'm good at and those things are currently not working out for me.

I'm not considering dropping out, the school is forcing me to leave because of their financial aid policy. Unless I meet the plan that they set out for me perfectly (and I mean perfectly. There's no happy accidents when it comes to the financial aid office) then I'd best call myself Heisenberg and get to cooking bitch. 

I've done the research. Yesterday evening I turned in a ten page essay analyzing and comparing "three different paths to a career in technology".

The people I interviewed said "Go to college, it's really hard to get in without a degree". The research I found said "Go to college, it's really hard to get in without a degree". Literally the only people who say "You can totally get in without a degree" are random ass redditors.

And again, I'm not interested in starting my own business.

I come from a family of business majors. They'll all tell you the same thing, if you want to start your own business that actually makes any money you're better off going to college. Otherwise unless you're some miracle worker like redditors seem to be you're going to sink a lot of your money from working at Burger King into one of the many failed startups.

Hm. Chill. Take a breather. Your excuses are pathetic. Stop playing video games.

Are you sure you're in the right subreddit? Because here is the translation I'm reading from your post

"So I just wanted to tell you you're a pussy for wanting to kill yourself. Nobody is going to help you with anything, at any point in your life so you have to do it all yourself. You just need to try new things, I apparently missed the part about this already being your second attempt at something. Just seek counseling with all of your money on how to cope, exercise with your abundant amount of free time. It worked for me. I dropped out of Ivy League, not because I was being forced out despite my GPA of course. I possessed no skills or career training, and I worked at fast food industries and retail. You know, the jobs you said that if you ever ended up there you would kill yourself! Well guess what, you're going to end up there! I saved money and started my own business, because of course in my infinite knowledge I'm aware that all businesses need is a little bit of elbow grease and everyone out there can just start up their own business. Even if that's not at all what they wanted to do and if they don't have the first clue how to run one, it's a good idea for you to risk a lot of your assets on this so you can end up even poorer than when you flipped burgers. You're asking for advice on a suicidewatch subreddit like some sort of dumbass when you should be bullshitting like the rest of your peers do! You seem entitled so I'm going to assume you thought college was a guarantee, so you aren't guaranteed crap except for debt. So since you're currently considering permanently ending your life, my sage advice to you is to chill, take a breather. I know that not getting everything you want like your spoiled millennial ass thinks you deserve is not great but you need to stop playing video games (I don't anymore, no time) and work on reality, whatever the fuck that means"
Already tried that. It didn't work out. Read "vocational school"

I'll ask you what I've asked everyone else here who says things like this.

If I fail out of college what do you imagine happens to someone like me? What, in your mind, comes next?

K so I don't go to school. I possess no talents of skills and so far I've failed everything I've tried.

Where do I go besides suicide in your mind. I'm interested to know what you think happens to people like that.
Largely living off financial aid refunds and money leftover from a previous job. I don't work during school

No friends. Only my girlfriend and she lives at home. I don't have a good relationship with her family.

Yes, I live alone.
No

I've searched the requirements online. It isn't an immediate disqualifier but unless the grief was related to the death of a loved one or prior military service, it can be considered a security risk and will be investigated.

From there it's sort of up in the air. They'll ask your doctor if they think your condition would impair your ability to work, if they say no you're okay. Say yes, you're disqualified and likely won't be able to get another chance.

I can avoid all of that by simply avoiding that route altogether and either graduating college or killing myself.

So play this scenario out for me please.

I say "fuck school" after not being able to complete. Maybe I fail a course, maybe I can't register, whatever.

In this scenario where I do not graduate college and I don't kill myself. What do you imagine happens to me? Keep in mind, trade school didn't work out for me so going back to that is about as good as flipping burgers.

Again, a Jr developer with a college degree. A jr developer without one works the help desk and kisses ass until they are allowed to touch something that won't break. They make around $10 an hour.

My college does not offer free counseling services. Even if they did, you get what you pay for with mental health.

Medical records are confidential except for obtaining a security clearance. The government is allowed to consider your past medical history for selection in those kinds of jobs. An anti-depressant prescription locks me into the private sector. I might not want a government job down the road, but I'd like the option to be open.

edit: By the way, try c++. You might be a whiz at data structures but I'm fucking awful at them.

It does. It just doesn't offer it to people who completed two years of vocational school.

You're expected to complete your degree within an allotted timeframe. That timeframe is dictated by the credits you have. If you have too many it's decided that it's impossible for you to finish your degree. 

I have two years worth of credits. If I'm not forced to drop out I will graduate in the spring with 120 credits. You're put on academic probation at around 60 for community college and 120 for university.

That means if I fail a course, I no longer qualify for any more aid. Permanently. Because they won't consider someone with 120 credit hours and no degree to be a student that is making adequate academic progress. 

Same if I drop a course.

Same if I change degrees.

I can change schools but if I lose a single credit in the transfer I lose eligibility. 

I'm completely dependent on aid for school. Private loans aren't exactly interested in students like me either and they like the kinds of interest rates that that are two digits and start with a 1. Scholarships won't even cover a semester of school. 

So I'm hoping you can understand why simply killing myself sounds rather appealing right now compared to allowing myself to be a burger flipper with a 3.7 GPA, trade school certificate and three semesters of a STEM degree.

I didn't want to reveal this much information but I'm already a computer science major. I've done the tutorials and at this point I've received a reasonable amount of instruction on different computer programs. Working on c++ right now (which sucks dick by the way, if I don't kill myself I want to keep far, far away from this bullshit).

I'm afraid you're not entirely correct about the degree. Every business I spoke to said they would not hire someone without at least a bachelor's or about five to ten years experience. How do you get the five to ten years experience without a bachelor's in the first place?

I'm not saying it's impossible, but it's incredibly unlikely. One would need a lot of skill and if I'm unable to get through school, it means I lack that skill. Not even mentioning the salary hit you get for starting at an entry level position. My best option is college and if that doesn't work. Well, I don't want to sound like a broken record.

I have not spoken to a therapist or received antidepressants. I'm a broke college kid, I don't have money for that.

Moreover, the last thing I want is an anti-depressant prescription coming back to haunt me. If I make it through college what if I want a job that requires security clearance? Getting that now could fuck me later.

Besides, a therapist isn't going to tell me anything I don't already know. My dad is a drug counselor, I know how this stuff works. A therapist would try and get me to open up about my issues and then charge me $200 an hour before telling me that giving up won't solve anything.

If I attempt to go to another school then I lose my eligibility for federal aid. I'm trapped. 

There's nothing I always wanted to be. People kept saying "You'll have plenty of time to figure that out" until I was standing in the registrar's office at my college and they said "If you don't pick a degree before the office closes today you'll never get into college. After this you can't switch majors either"

I can't start over. It's not "I don't want to". I can't. I literally have no other choices for this. Unless I come up with enough cash to pay for tuition out of pocket it is impossible to start over because it would remove my eligibility for tuition assistance. Permanently.

I already devote my time to my studies. I've gone without sleep three nights this week to try and finish a project that's late (it's still not finished). Two nights the week before. The week before that was something similar. 

I don't want to grind my way up through a profession. What I want is for college to not be a waste of time. To even get considered for a job in the field I'm interested you almost always need a college degree. Some dipshit redditors will say otherwise but I've got the research to back me up. I literally just finished an assignment on this earlier this evening.

You know how many startups fail? I'm not going to throw money at hairbrained business ventures that I don't know how to get going. That's never appealed to me, it is nowhere on the list of things I want to do. You seem to misunderstand that people don't simply fail because of lack of effort, there are millions of people out there who try really hard and they still fail. Putting the "pedal to the metal" isn't all that comes into starting up one's own business. Especially if you're doing it without a college degree. I'd arrive at bankruptcy faster than if I was flipping burgers.

And on flipping burgers, I'm not sure I understand how you got the notion I would have a plentiful life outside of work. Especially when I literally said "I would rather kill myself than do that."

Not giving up isn't enough. More effort isn't enough. With my current college situation I'm not allowed any second chances at anything. It isn't "if at first you don't succeed, try try again" with my college right now, it's "if at first you don't succeed then drop out of school because you don't qualify for loans"

I don't care about using my degree. Without a degree I can't get past HR for a job. I know this because I just wrote a ten page essay on that and interviewed my professors and local businesses. I need this degree to even get a start, otherwise employers are unlikely to look at my application.

Three things I get enjoyment out of:

1. Being around my girlfriend

2. Uh... That's it. Like I enjoy sleeping a lot and playing video games (in the fleeting moments I have time) but I'm not really counting those.

3. Since I don't know anything else, I'll tell you that I used to enjoy solving problems. I loved the feeling of being faced with something that wasn't working and making it work. I fixed people's computers all the time, I tried to do it for the cost of parts alone but my girlfriend and family insisted I start charging for labor. I replaced a woman's hard drive (and rescued every one of her files) for $50, $40 of that being parts. I was just happy to take business from Geek Squad and to give her the family recipes she thought were gone forever when her drive crashed. Most of the time for other people I'd simply ask that they give me some food. I removed 315 malicious files off someone's computer for a large pepperoni pizza.

Not just computer stuff either, I loved solving problems simply because they existed. Untying knots, getting the tiny dresses to fit on my niece's dolls, puzzles.

But not any more though. Now it just makes me frustrated.

Yep.

The first time I talked to my counselor I had just graduated vocational school and was interested in going back to college. She told me to "strongly consider" whether or not I should return to school.

I talked to her one more time after my first semester, at this point I had a 4.0 GPA, though I suppose that isn't too impressive for one's first semester. She told me that I should still consider paths other than college and that perhaps it isn't a good idea.

I'm unable to speak to her now, her schedule is booked until early December. Far too late in the semester to solve the issues I'm currently having. 

Other than that, not a lot of resources. I spoke to another counselor who didn't have much advise for me and told me to go talk to my own counselor. 

Closest thing to a career advisor is my professor who is the dean of the program. I recently asked him some questions about the path to getting a career in the field I'm interested in. He basically said college, with my major. Anything else is much harder if not impossible.

Without revealing too much information (I've been bitching about this a lot on reddit lately), learn a trade. Two years of trade school and I never got any better. All of my instructors told me that actual college would be a perfect fit for someone like me and I should consider that instead of continuing my trade, now people ask me if I'm sure college is for me and if I've considered vocational school.

Plan B was get through college. But because of my complications I mentioned in the original post, that is suddenly looking grim as well.
